title: Workpaper
description: A workpaper is a documented working file that supports a position taken in an engagement - for example a lead schedule, an account reconciliation, a tax-position memo, or a supporting calculation. It records what the file is, who prepared and reviewed it, its sign-off state, the source documents it relies on, and an optional tie-out figure. This is a vocabulary for describing and exchanging workpapers, not a computation engine: the figures it carries are recorded, not derived by the spec.

engagementId.description: Identifier of the engagement this workpaper belongs to.

reference.description: Short index reference for the workpaper within the engagement file, e.g. "A-1", "1100", "B.3". Indexing schemes are firm-specific; the spec only carries the label.

title.description: Human-readable title, e.g. "Cash lead schedule", "Operating account reconciliation - May".

kind.description: The nature of the workpaper. Firm-agnostic vocabulary; use 'other' plus the title for anything outside this list.

status.description: Sign-off lifecycle of the workpaper. The canonical flow is not_started -> in_progress -> prepared -> reviewed -> finalized; 'reopened' marks a finalized paper sent back for changes.

period.description: The reporting period the workpaper covers, when narrower than the engagement period.

preparedBy.description: The person who prepared the workpaper.

reviewedBy.description: The person who reviewed and signed off the workpaper. Present once status reaches reviewed or beyond.

tieOut.description: An optional record of the amount this workpaper ties out to (for example the balance a reconciliation agrees to) and whether the two sides agree. The spec records the figures and the flag; it does not compute or verify them.

balance.description: The amount the workpaper supports (e.g. the per-books or per-statement balance).

supportingTotal.description: The total of the supporting detail being tied to the balance.

agrees.description: Whether the two figures agree, as asserted by the preparer/reviewer. Recorded, not derived.

sources.description: Source documents the workpaper relies on (statements, exports, prior-year papers).

requestItemIds.description: Identifiers of request-list items whose receipt this workpaper depends on, linking the client-side chase loop to the working file.

notes.description: Free-text annotations and review points on the workpaper.
